newsitem.title: INDIA: Polls mark new start for India's troubled Punjab.
newsitem.headline: Polls mark new start for India's troubled Punjab.

text.p: Voters in India's nothern state of Punjab will elect a new government on Friday in what are expected to be the first peaceful assembly polls since 1977.
Following is a chronology of political landmarks, assassinations and major outbreaks of separatist violence in the rich farming region over the past two decades:
April 1978 - Thirteen members of the Sikh Akhand Kirtani Jatha killed in clash with rival Nirankari sect during the rule of the pro-separatist Sikh Akali Dal party
1979 - Akali Dal government dismissed by New Delhi, leading to sporadic violence
1981 - Congress government elected despite threats by Sikh militants. Sporadic vioence continues.
1984 - Congress government dismissed following the massacre of several bus passengers in Punjab, mostly Hindu.

June 1984 - Indian army storms the Golden Temple in Amritsar, the Sikhs' holiest shrine, to flush out armed Sikh militants, killing about 1,000 people. The assault shocks Sikhs, who see it as a desecration.
October 31, 1984 - Prime Minister Indira Gandhi assassinated at her residence in New Delhi by two Sikh bodyguards.
November 1984 - Nearly 3,000 people hacked or burnt to death, mostly in Delhi, during anti-Sikh riots.
May 1985 - Sikh extremists set off bombs in and around Delhi, killing 86 people.
June 1985 - An Air-India flight explodes and crashes into the sea off the coast of Ireland, killing 329 people. Sikh extremists claim responsibility.
August 1985 - Harchand Singh Longowal, who as the head of the main Sikh political party signed a peace accord with New Delhi, is gunned down by extremist militants in Punjab.
August 1986 - Four Sikh guerrillas gun down General Arun Vaidya, Army Chief during the 1984 Golden Temple assault, in Pune, Maharashtra state.
October 1986 - Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi survives an attempt on his life by a Sikh in New Delhi at the spot where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated.
July 1987 - Sikh gunmen massacre 70 Hindus in Delhi.
June 1989 - Sikh militants gun down 24 fundamentalist Hindus who were exercising in a Punjab park.
November 1989 - Sikh militants kill 21 students outside a college near Amritsar.
April 1990 - Militants bomb Hindu procession in Punjab, killing 32.
June 1990 - About 30 people killed in sectarian violence on the sixth anniversary of the Indian army assault on the Golden Temple.
March and July 1991 - Punjab governor escapes two assassination attempts by Sikh guerrillas.
February 1992 - Congress wins state elections after the Akali Dal boycotts polls.
August 31, 1995 - Punjab's Congress Chief Minister Beant Singh killed with 12 others in car bomb in Chandigarh.
